title: Idempotent payments stack — four PRs, three reviewers
verdict: Illustrative: hold #413 and #414 until the duplicate-charge race and retry key are fixed.
summary: Demo data for a stacked-PR review of a fictional repository. It shows how the report presents a PR hierarchy, per-PR findings, disagreements, and reviewer provenance. None of these findings describe real code.

target.Stack: 4 PRs on main: #412 → #413 → #414, with #416 forked from #413
target.Comparison: Each PR against its parent branch; findings are attributed to the PR that introduces the root cause
target.Scope: Full diffs plus touched callers, migrations, and worker configuration
target.Rounds: Independent first pass, then one targeted round for F-004 and F-010

findings.title: Concurrent requests with one key can both charge the card
findings.trigger: Two POST /payments requests with the same Idempotency-Key arrive within the gateway round-trip (client retry on timeout).
findings.impact: Both requests miss the lookup, both call the gateway, and the customer is charged twice.
findings.evidence:
key = IdempotencyKey.find_by(key: header)
return replay(key) if key
result = Gateway.charge!(params)   # no row exists yet
IdempotencyKey.create!(key: header, response: result)
findings.recommendation: Insert the key row in a `processing` state first (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and only call the gateway when this request won the insert.
findings.decision: Confirmed by coordinator with a two-thread reproduction against the demo schema.

findings.title: Unique index omits merchant_id, so keys collide across merchants
findings.trigger: Two merchants independently send the same UUID-like key (common with client libraries that hash request bodies).
findings.impact: The second merchant receives the first merchant's cached response, leaking payment metadata across tenants.
findings.recommendation: Scope the unique index and all lookups to (merchant_id, key).
findings.decision: Confirmed; every lookup in #413 also omits merchant_id.

findings.title: Each retry sends a fresh idempotency key to the gateway
findings.trigger: A capture times out after the gateway accepted it, then the worker retries.
findings.impact: Gateway-side deduplication is defeated, so a slow-but-successful capture can be captured again.
findings.recommendation: Derive the gateway key from the payment and attempt series (for example `capture:#{payment.id}`) and reuse it on every retry.
findings.decision: Confirmed; all three reviewers found it independently.

findings.title: Retry job can capture after the payment was voided
findings.trigger: A merchant voids the payment while a retry is waiting in backoff.
findings.impact: The worker does not reload the payment before capturing, so a voided payment may still be captured.
findings.evidence:
def perform(payment_id, attempt)
  payment = Payment.find(payment_id)   # loaded once before sleep_for(attempt)
  sleep_for(attempt)
  capture!(payment)
findings.recommendation: Reload with a row lock after the backoff and skip unless the payment is still `authorized`.
findings.decision: Plausible from inspection; whether the gateway rejects captures on voided authorizations is unverified.
findings.validation: No gateway sandbox run. Needs a check against the gateway's void semantics.

findings.title: Cached 5xx responses are replayed forever
findings.trigger: The gateway returns 503 once; the client retries with the same key.
findings.impact: Codex: the stored 503 is replayed on every retry, so the payment can never succeed with that key.
findings.evidence: Codex cites `IdempotencyKey.create!(response: result)` storing any status. Claude Code cites `ensure key.release! if result.server_error?` deleting 5xx rows.
findings.recommendation: Store only terminal 2xx/4xx responses, and release the row explicitly on 5xx, including after crashes.
findings.decision: Disputed. The ensure block releases rows on normal 5xx returns, but not when the process is killed mid-request; then the `processing` row never expires.
findings.validation: Round 2: Claude Code disagreed, Cursor timed out. Needs a crash-injection test.

findings.title: TTL cleanup deletes keys that are still processing
findings.trigger: A request remains in `processing` for longer than the 24-hour TTL (stuck worker, gateway outage).
findings.impact: The cleanup job in #412 deletes the row that #413 uses as its lock, reopening the duplicate-charge window.
findings.recommendation: Only expire rows in a terminal state, and alert on rows stuck in `processing`.
findings.decision: Confirmed; the problem appears only when #412 and #413 are combined.

findings.title: Retry exhaustion leaves captures in `retrying` without an alert
findings.impact: The payment stays in `retrying` and nobody is notified; funds remain authorized until the hold expires.
findings.evidence: return if attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS   # silent exit
findings.recommendation: Move the payment to `capture_failed`, emit a metric, and page on a nonzero rate.

findings.title: Request fingerprint depends on JSON key order
findings.trigger: A client retries with the same body, serialized with a different key order.
findings.impact: The retry is rejected with 422 `key reused with different payload` even though the payload is identical.
findings.recommendation: Fingerprint a canonicalized parsed body, or document byte-identical retries as a requirement.
findings.decision: Likely real; impact depends on which SDKs reorder keys.
findings.validation: Not exercised against the official client SDKs.

findings.title: Runbook tells on-call to delete idempotency rows by hand
findings.impact: Manually deleting a `processing` row reopens the F-001 duplicate-charge window for in-flight retries.
findings.evidence: > If a payment is stuck, run `IdempotencyKey.where(key: ...).delete_all` and ask the merchant to retry.
findings.recommendation: Replace the deletion with a state transition that refuses rows younger than the gateway timeout.

findings.title: Missing Idempotency-Key returns 400 without a problem+json body
findings.impact: The response is inconsistent with every other 4xx in the API, which breaks typed client error handling.
findings.recommendation: Render the standard problem+json error with a stable `type` URI.

findings.title: Alert threshold uses p50 rather than p99 latency
findings.trigger: Gateway latency degrades for a minority of requests.
findings.impact: Tail latency that causes client timeouts and retries would not page anyone.
findings.recommendation: Alert on p99 (or the client timeout budget) instead.
findings.decision: Unvalidated; the alert definition lives outside this repository.
findings.validation: The alerting repository was not in scope.

findings.title: Built-in and custom retries double-schedule jobs
findings.impact: Cursor Agent: the queue's automatic retry and the custom backoff would both enqueue a retry.
findings.evidence: ApplicationWorker sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`; CaptureRetryWorker inherits it.
findings.decision: Rejected: the base class disables built-in retries, and Codex and Claude Code agreed in round 2.

findings.title: Migration locks the payments table
findings.impact: Codex: adding a foreign key to payments would take a lock that blocks writes.
findings.decision: Rejected: the foreign key is created NOT VALID, which does not scan or block payments writes.

checks: Coordinator static inspection of all four PR diffs and touched callers (illustrative).
Two-thread reproduction of F-001 against a local copy of the demo schema (illustrative).
No CI, gateway sandbox, or deployed checks were run for this demo.
gaps: Demo data: every finding, check, and reviewer run on this page is illustrative.
Cursor Agent did not complete the targeted round 2, so F-004 has two of three reviewer opinions.
Alert definitions for F-012 live in a separate repository that was not reviewed.
next_steps: Fix F-001 and F-002 in #412/#413 before rebasing the rest of the stack.
Reuse a stable gateway key in #414 (F-013), then re-review the worker.
Add a crash-injection test to settle F-004.

notes.title: Read the stack bottom-up
notes.body: Fixes in #412 change what #413, #414, and #416 inherit. Use “Include lower PRs” to see every finding that affects a PR you are about to merge.

notes.title: Answer, then copy
notes.body: Every finding starts as Fix. Ignore the ones you do not want fixed, comment where needed, then use Copy answers to hand the JSON to the agent. Answers and pins stay in this browser and never change the report file.
